scenes.heading: Angles and parallel lines
scenes.sub: Know one angle, find all eight
scenes.say: When a road crosses two train tracks, it makes eight angles. Here's the amazing part: if you know just one of them, you can find all the others.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Copy and paste the same pattern further along
scenes.science: The 4 angles at each parallel line are identical copies
scenes.breaks: it only works if the lines are exactly parallel. Tilt one line and the two patterns are different.
scenes.say: Think of copy and paste. Where the road crosses the first track, it makes a pattern of four angles. Because the tracks point the same way, that pattern is copied and pasted at the second track. But it only works if the lines are exactly parallel.
scenes.caption: Where the road crosses the first track, it makes a pattern of four angles. Because the tracks are parallel, that pattern is copied and pasted at the second track.

scenes.heading: F, Z and C
points: A transversal crosses the parallel lines
scenes.say: The line crossing the parallel lines is called a transversal. Look for three letter shapes. In an F, corresponding angles are equal. In a Z, alternate angles are equal. In a C, co-interior angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees.
scenes.caption: The crossing line is a transversal. In an F, corresponding angles are equal. In a Z, alternate angles are equal. In a C, co-interior angles add to 180°.

scenes.heading: Alternate angles: the Z shape
scenes.say: First two parallel lines with their arrows, then a transversal cutting across. Between the lines, on opposite sides of the transversal, sit two angles. Trace them and you get a Z. Alternate angles are equal, so the missing angle is one hundred and eight degrees.
scenes.caption: Between the lines, on opposite sides of the transversal: a Z shape. Alternate angles are equal, so the missing angle is 108°.

scenes.heading: Co-interior angles: the C shape
scenes.say: Same lines again. This time both angles are between the lines, on the same side of the transversal: one hundred and eighteen and y. They make a C shape, so they add to one hundred and eighty. y is sixty-two.
scenes.caption: Both angles are between the lines, on the same side: 118° and y. A C shape, so they add to 180°. y = 62°.

scenes.heading: Alternate vs co-interior
scenes.say: Both of these are between the parallel lines, so don't mix them up. Alternate angles are on opposite sides of the transversal, and they're equal. Co-interior angles are on the same side, and they add to one hundred and eighty. C for combine!
scenes.caption: Both are between the parallel lines. Alternate angles are on opposite sides of the transversal, and they're equal. Co-interior angles are on the same side, and they add to 180°. C for combine!

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Two co-interior angles between parallel lines are x° and (x + 20)°. Find x.
scenes.say: Two co-interior angles are x and x plus twenty. They add to one hundred and eighty, so two x plus twenty equals one hundred and eighty. Take away twenty: two x equals one hundred and sixty. So x is eighty. Check: eighty plus one hundred is one hundred and eighty.
scenes.caption: Two co-interior angles are x and x + 20. So 2x + 20 = 180. Take away 20: 2x = 160. So x = 80. Check: 80 + 100 = 180.

scenes.heading: Are they parallel?
scenes.question: Two co-interior angles are 95° and 80°. Are the lines parallel?
scenes.say: The rules also work backwards. Two co-interior angles are ninety-five and eighty degrees. They add to one hundred and seventy-five, not one hundred and eighty. So the lines are not parallel.
scenes.caption: The rules also work backwards. Two co-interior angles are 95° and 80°. They add to 175°, not 180°. So the lines are not parallel.

points: Only two angle sizes, adding to 180°
scenes.say: Quick recap. F angles are equal. Z angles are equal. C angles add to one hundred and eighty. And with parallel lines, there are only two sizes of angle. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. F angles are equal. Z angles are equal. C angles add to 180°. With parallel lines, there are only two sizes of angle. Now try the practice questions!
